questions.question: Explain who Psychological First Aid (PFA) is meant for. Describe the groups of people who may benefit from PFA. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain who Psychological First Aid (PFA) is meant for. Describe the groups of
  • people who may benefit from PFA. [U] / [CO2]
  • Psychological First Aid (PFA) is an evidence-informed, humane, and supportive initial
  • response to a fellow human being who is suffering after a crisis event and may need support.
  • It is designed for anyone who has been exposed to a serious crisis event. The core principle of
  • PFA is to provide practical care and support in a non-intrusive manner, without being
  • intrusive or pathologizing the person's distress. The groups of people who may benefit from
  • PFA are diverse and include: Survivors of Natural Disasters, Survivors of Human-Induced
  • Disasters, Victims of Violence and Assault, Children and Adolescents, First Responders and
  • Aid Workers , Individuals Who Have Lost Loved Ones and Community Members in the
  • Aftermath of a Crisis. Explain each one. Mention examples.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: A student who was a top performer in school now feels average in college. Using concepts of self-concept and social comparison, explain why this change occurred and how the student can improve their self-view. / [CO1] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• A student who was a top performer in school now feels average in college. Using
  • concepts of self-concept and social comparison, explain why this change occurred
  • and how the student can improve their self-view. [A] / [CO1]
  • Define self - concept, self – comparison. Leon Festinger’s- Social Comparison Theory
  • can be used to substantiate the answer. This situation shows how changes in the social
  • environment influence self-concept. In school, the student saw himself/herself as a “top
  • performer” because he/she compared their performance to the classmates. In college, the
  • comparison group changed to other high-achieving students, leading to upward social
  • comparison, which made the student feel average.
  • Some points to improving self-view:
  • • Focus on personal growth instead of comparing with others.
  • • Develop a broader self-concept through different activities.
  • • Adopt a growth mindset and see challenges as learning opportunities.
  • • Set personal and process-oriented goals.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
